records.title: AI receptionist return on investment: a net-value worksheet
records.description: Evaluate an AI receptionist using incremental job contribution, full service costs and a baseline. Use a worksheet without assuming every call becomes revenue.
records.lead: An AI receptionist return-on-investment calculation should answer a purchasing question: does the additional value your business can reasonably attribute to the service exceed its full cost? Answered calls, appointment requests and gross job value are useful observations, but none is the final return. records.intro: An AI receptionist return-on-investment calculation should answer a purchasing question: does the additional value your business can reasonably attribute to the service exceed its full cost? Answered calls, appointment requests and gross job value are useful observations, but none is the final return. Start with a defined alternative, the work you can actually accept and the costs that change with the decision.

sections.title: Choose the alternative you are comparing
paragraphs:
Write the decision at the top of the sheet: for example, adding answering coverage to the current office process. Describe what happens without the purchase, including callbacks your team already makes. A customer who would have booked after a callback is not automatically an additional job created by the new service.

Use one evaluation window and allow the same time for inquiries to become completed work. Keep a second column for assumptions when you do not yet have an observed comparison. A forecast can support a decision, but labeling an assumed lift as measured performance makes the result less useful.

sections.title: Use contribution from additional work, not the entire invoice
paragraphs:
For each additional completed job in your scenario, subtract the job costs that increase because you accept that work. These may include parts, consumables, incremental labor, subcontracting, travel and payment charges. Use the costs applicable to your operation rather than a generic margin benchmark.

The amount left is contribution toward service costs and the rest of the business. It is not the same as company net profit. Do not subtract the same job expense again as an answering-service expense. If an extra booking displaces another job your crew would otherwise have completed, account for the displaced contribution too. A full calendar can make additional inquiries valuable for selection without producing additional completed work.

sections.title: Copy this decision worksheet
paragraphs:
Fill in amounts for the same period. Retain the source or assumption beside each entry. Leave an unknown value unresolved rather than replacing it with an industry average.

| Entry | What belongs here | Your amount and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Additional completed-job contribution | Contribution from incremental completed work, after its incremental job costs and any displaced contribution | ______ |
| B. Avoided cash expense | An expense that actually disappears because of this decision | ______ |
| C. Recurring service expense | Subscription, expected billable usage and required recurring add-ons | ______ |
| D. Retained operating expense | Additional paid time or external expense for review, corrections and handoff that is not already in A | ______ |
| E. One-time launch expense | Setup charges and additional paid implementation work | ______ |
| F. Recurring net benefit | A + B − C − D | ______ |
| G. First-period net benefit | F − E | ______ |
| H. First-period decision return | G ÷ (C + D + E) × 100, only when the denominator is positive | ______ |

This worksheet defines its return denominator explicitly so two options can be compared consistently. It does not measure a company's total profitability. If the denominator is zero, report the amounts separately; do not display an infinite percentage.

sections.title: Check the arithmetic with a fictional case
paragraphs:
Suppose additional completed work contributes $600 after its incremental job costs. The business avoids no cash expense. Subscription and usage cost $200 for the period, additional paid operating work costs $100, and launch work costs $300 once. These are fictional inputs, not Revo prices or typical outcomes.

Recurring net benefit is $600 − $200 − $100 = $300. First-period net benefit is $300 − $300 = $0. The defined first-period return is $0 ÷ $600 = 0%. The $600 contribution is therefore not a $600 return after implementation costs.

If the same recurring assumptions held, the $300 launch expense would take one period of positive $300 recurring net benefit to recover. That is a scenario, not a promised payback date. A zero or negative recurring net benefit does not yield a finite positive payback period under those assumptions.

sections.title: Keep time savings and cash savings separate
paragraphs:
Owner time released from answering calls can matter even when payroll does not change. Record those hours and the work you intend to do with them. Do not automatically add an hourly valuation to avoided payroll and also count the contribution from jobs performed in the same hours. That would count one benefit twice.

Run a lower-demand case as well as your expected case. Reduce additional completed work, increase paid usage or allow more office review. Ask whether the purchase remains affordable when the upside is smaller. Keep service quality and follow-up ownership alongside the calculation; a positive spreadsheet result does not establish that the answering workflow is suitable.

sections.title: Compare the supported Revo scope before entering a price
paragraphs:
Use [Revo's current pricing](/pricing) for the actual plan and included usage, and confirm the setup needed for your business. Revo publishes AI answering, intake, appointment booking and summaries; team transfers and other features depend on the plan and supported configuration. A qualified inquiry is not a completed job, and booking does not establish dispatch or collected revenue.

Use the [cost-of-missed-calls worksheet](/ai-answering-service/cost-of-missed-calls) when you need a gross opportunity scenario. Use the [conversion comparison guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-conversion-rate-comparison) to define comparable inquiry cohorts. Bring those inputs here only after deciding which outcomes and costs belong in the purchase decision.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Is every answered call additional revenue?

No. Calls may be duplicates, existing-customer questions or inquiries that your office would have recovered anyway. Separate answered calls from incremental completed work.

### Can I count the owner's released time?

Record it separately unless it produces an identifiable cash saving or additional contribution. Avoid counting both the time valuation and the value created during those same hours.

### Is the calculated return guaranteed?

No. The result depends on the baseline, attribution, capacity and cost inputs you supply. Keep forecast assumptions separate from observed records and update the decision when evidence changes.

### What should I do if I cannot estimate additional completed jobs?

Leave the benefit unknown. Compare the service's affordability and supported workflow, then define what evidence a limited evaluation would need to collect. Do not invent a conversion lift to make the purchase look attractive.

Review [Revo's plans and included usage](/pricing), then complete the worksheet with your own operating records before choosing coverage.

An AI receptionist return-on-investment calculation should answer a purchasing question: does the additional value your business can reasonably attribute to the service exceed its full cost? Answered calls, appointment requests and gross job value are useful observations, but none is the final return. Start with a defined alternative, the work you can actually accept and the costs that change with the decision.

Published by Revo, a provider of AI answering services. This is a planning worksheet, not a claim about customer results or a guarantee of savings.

## Choose the alternative you are comparing

Write the decision at the top of the sheet: for example, adding answering coverage to the current office process. Describe what happens without the purchase, including callbacks your team already makes. A customer who would have booked after a callback is not automatically an additional job created by the new service.

Use one evaluation window and allow the same time for inquiries to become completed work. Keep a second column for assumptions when you do not yet have an observed comparison. A forecast can support a decision, but labeling an assumed lift as measured performance makes the result less useful.

## Use contribution from additional work, not the entire invoice

For each additional completed job in your scenario, subtract the job costs that increase because you accept that work. These may include parts, consumables, incremental labor, subcontracting, travel and payment charges. Use the costs applicable to your operation rather than a generic margin benchmark.

The amount left is contribution toward service costs and the rest of the business. It is not the same as company net profit. Do not subtract the same job expense again as an answering-service expense. If an extra booking displaces another job your crew would otherwise have completed, account for the displaced contribution too. A full calendar can make additional inquiries valuable for selection without producing additional completed work.

## Copy this decision worksheet

Fill in amounts for the same period. Retain the source or assumption beside each entry. Leave an unknown value unresolved rather than replacing it with an industry average.

| Entry | What belongs here | Your amount and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |

| D. Retained operating expense | Additional paid time or external expense for review, corrections and handoff that is not already in A | ______ |
| E. One-time launch expense | Setup charges and additional paid implementation work | ______ |
| F. Recurring net benefit | A + B − C − D | ______ |
| G. First-period net benefit | F − E | ______ |
| H. First-period decision return | G ÷ (C + D + E) × 100, only when the denominator is positive | ______ |

This worksheet defines its return denominator explicitly so two options can be compared consistently. It does not measure a company's total profitability. If the denominator is zero, report the amounts separately; do not display an infinite percentage.

## Check the arithmetic with a fictional case

Suppose additional completed work contributes $600 after its incremental job costs. The business avoids no cash expense. Subscription and usage cost $200 for the period, additional paid operating work costs $100, and launch work costs $300 once. These are fictional inputs, not Revo prices or typical outcomes.

Recurring net benefit is $600 − $200 − $100 = $300. First-period net benefit is $300 − $300 = $0. The defined first-period return is $0 ÷ $600 = 0%. The $600 contribution is therefore not a $600 return after implementation costs.

If the same recurring assumptions held, the $300 launch expense would take one period of positive $300 recurring net benefit to recover. That is a scenario, not a promised payback date. A zero or negative recurring net benefit does not yield a finite positive payback period under those assumptions.

## Keep time savings and cash savings separate

Owner time released from answering calls can matter even when payroll does not change. Record those hours and the work you intend to do with them. Do not automatically add an hourly valuation to avoided payroll and also count the contribution from jobs performed in the same hours. That would count one benefit twice.

Run a lower-demand case as well as your expected case. Reduce additional completed work, increase paid usage or allow more office review. Ask whether the purchase remains affordable when the upside is smaller. Keep service quality and follow-up ownership alongside the calculation; a positive spreadsheet result does not establish that the answering workflow is suitable.

## Compare the supported Revo scope before entering a price

Use [Revo's current pricing](/pricing) for the actual plan and included usage, and confirm the setup needed for your business. Revo publishes AI answering, intake, appointment booking and summaries; team transfers and other features depend on the plan and supported configuration. A qualified inquiry is not a completed job, and booking does not establish dispatch or collected revenue.

Use the [cost-of-missed-calls worksheet](/ai-answering-service/cost-of-missed-calls) when you need a gross opportunity scenario. Use the [conversion comparison guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-conversion-rate-comparison) to define comparable inquiry cohorts. Bring those inputs here only after deciding which outcomes and costs belong in the purchase decision.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is every answered call additional revenue?

No. Calls may be duplicates, existing-customer questions or inquiries that your office would have recovered anyway. Separate answered calls from incremental completed work.

### Can I count the owner's released time?

sections.title: Start with Phone, then examine the larger product separately
paragraphs:

Start with the [Phone product page](https://www.beside.com/phone) and its plan page. Write the exact product, purchase channel, billing unit and included reception allowance on your comparison sheet. sections.title: Identify the offer available to your signup route
paragraphs:
Beside's [Phone pricing page](https://www.beside.com/phone/pricing) lists web plans billed monthly per business and separately describes some mobile subscriptions billed per seat. It also distinguishes the AI-receptionist allowance from ordinary calling and texting. Those are material differences; a general “unlimited calls” phrase does not tell you the reception allowance for every offer.

The purchase screen and applicable terms should settle the offer for your account, country and signup channel. Record whether a trial is offered, when billing starts and where cancellation is managed. A free app download is not evidence of free ongoing reception. sections.title: Build a decision record around your actual business line
paragraphs:
Copy the table below for each option. Complete the evidence column from the provider's applicable plan and a demonstration using fictional caller details. Unresolved items should stay unresolved until the supplier confirms them.

| Decision | Evidence to obtain | Office action before starting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Number arrangement | New number, forwarding or porting route supported for this account | Identify who controls the existing number and approves changes |
| Calls the AI answers | Primary answering, missed-call coverage or another configured rule | Define the intended ringing and fallback behavior |
| Reception allowance | What counts as an AI-handled call and what happens at the allowance | Compare against your own eligible call mix |
| Booking outcome | Supported calendar, approved availability and confirmation behavior | Separate a confirmed slot from a requested time |
| Human handoff | Supported destination, plan and unavailable-contact outcome | Name the person responsible for exceptions |
| Account ownership | Billing administrator, team access and purchase channel | Keep business ownership clear if staff change |
| End of service | Number arrangements, supported exports and cancellation process | Document a handback plan before changing a live line |

Forwarding and porting are different operating decisions. Do not cancel the current carrier or move a number simply to evaluate a receptionist. Agree the supported route, responsibilities and return path first.

sections.title: Check how the receptionist uses your instructions
paragraphs:
Beside's [receptionist guidance](https://help.beside.com/en/articles/14602839-get-the-most-out-of-your-receptionist) recommends specific business knowledge, boundaries on what the receptionist should say, scenario questions and repeated testing. For a residential service company, translate that into your real service area, approved work categories and unresolved-request owner.

Use three fictional calls with different outcomes. A new customer asks for a service you perform: does the record retain the property area and requested work? An existing customer asks a technical question about an active job: does it reach the right person without an invented answer? A caller asks for an unavailable appointment: does the response accurately distinguish a request from a confirmed booking?

Record the observed outcome and the setup used. One successful demonstration does not establish performance for every caller, accent, connection or exception. Do not use real customer records to make a comparison easier.

sections.title: Compare the reception purchase with Revo's supported scope
paragraphs:
Beside Phone may be relevant when you want a business-phone app together with reception and conversation context. That combined product scope is a valid reason to evaluate it. Revo's answering offer should be assessed on its own published terms rather than presented as an equivalent replacement for every Phone or broader Beside feature.

Revo publishes AI answering, intake, appointment booking and call summaries. Team transfers and other features depend on the plan and supported configuration. No Beside integration, phone-number migration, shared inbox, business-agent workflow or other function is established for Revo by this comparison.

Review [Revo's current plans](/pricing), then compare only the tasks your office needs. If a full business-phone application or a specific connected tool is essential, verify that requirement explicitly with each provider. A lower subscription price alone does not settle a scope mismatch.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Is M1 a separate product from Beside?

The current US App Store identifies the application as Beside (M1): AI Receptionist. Follow current Beside Phone documentation for today's product rather than assuming an older M1 description is still the applicable offer.

### Are all Beside subscription offers identical?

No. The current Phone pricing page distinguishes web plans from certain mobile subscription arrangements. Confirm your own product, channel, currency, unit and reception allowance.

### Does choosing an AI receptionist require changing my number?

Do not assume that it does. Obtain the provider's account-specific options for forwarding, a new number or porting, and keep control of the existing line while evaluating the service.

### Does Revo include everything described on Beside's site?

This guide makes no such claim. Compare Revo's documented answering scope with the particular Phone or business-agent offer you are considering.

[Review Revo's plans and included usage](/pricing) with your completed call-workflow decision record.
